removability.rationale: Deleting the route directory gets you most of the way; the only entanglement is the spec-mandated Abilities section on the Pokémon page and the paired `abilityPage` helper, all grep-able with one search for 'abilit'.

evidence: app/src/lib/data.ts:23 — spriteUrl is the single sprite-URL constructor for two of three card sites
app/src/lib/data.ts:81 — cardsForPokemon builds cards for move/ability/type pages
app/src/lib/data.ts:139-140 — homePage builds cards separately (duplicate construction)
app/src/lib/data.ts:432 — teamPage builds a third card variant using pokemon.sprites.front_default instead of spriteUrl
app/src/lib/format.ts:1-46 — humanize/dexNumber/flavor helpers centralized, one obvious home for text fixes
changeability.rationale: Most page-level fixes land in exactly one function per page (homePage/pokemonPage/movePage...), and text formatting is fully centralized. But the sprite-fix scenario shows the card shape is built in three places in one file, so a card-level fix is two or three edits rather than one.

evidence: app/src/lib/api.ts:1-74 — transport and caching isolated behind get/find; nothing else knows about fetch or the cache
app/src/lib/data.ts:1-3 — 'Server only' module comment; routes only consume the returned plain objects
app/src/lib/team.ts:36-48 — cookie DOM code deliberately kept out of the server-only module, with a comment explaining why
app/src/components/ui.tsx:4 — components import Card/EvolutionNode types from lib/data (type-only, erased at build, but couples component types to the server module)
app/src/routes/layout.tsx:5-8 — cache-control policy declared once for all pages
coupling.rationale: Layering is genuinely clean: routes depend on narrow, serializable page objects; server/client state (the team cookie) is explicit and documented. Minor tangles: ui components typing themselves off the server data module, and data.ts being a shared god module every route imports from.

evidence: app/src/components/ui.tsx:35-42 — CardList/PokemonCard reused by home, moves, abilities and types pages
app/src/components/move-table.tsx:1-30 — MoveTable is a generic sortable table driven by data, no per-page copy
app/src/components/ui.tsx:4-33 — Section/TypeBadge small composable primitives; TypeBadge's `link?: boolean` is mild flag creep
app/src/lib/data.ts:74-83 — cardsForPokemon already models the real variation (extra callback for hidden-ability flagging) instead of duplicating filtering
app/src/routes/moves/[name]/index.tsx:5-33 — route skeleton (loader/status 404/NotFound/head) is ~30 lines that would be copied for an Items section
abstraction_design.rationale: The components stretch well: an Items page would reuse Section, TypeBadge, CardList, orDash, pageTitle and the loader pattern, copying only the thin route file and adding an itemPage builder. Cost: the per-route boilerplate is inherently duplicated Qwik City code, and card construction (the app's one shared data shape) isn't abstracted to a single factory.

findings.issue: Pokémon Card objects are constructed in three places (cardsForPokemon:81, homePage:139, teamPage:432), so changes to card shape — sprite rules, sorting, new fields — must be made three times, and teamPage already diverges (uses front_default instead of spriteUrl).
findings.suggestion: Extract a single card factory (e.g. makeCard(id, speciesName, extra)) or make homePage/teamPage build their cards through cardsForPokemon-style shared code, so every card list shares one construction path.

findings.issue: data.ts is a 449-line module holding the server data builders for every page (home, pokemon, moves, abilities, types, team), which every route imports from.
findings.suggestion: Split per domain (lib/pages/pokemon.ts, moves.ts, types.ts, team.ts) keeping shared helpers (speciesById, cardsForPokemon, typeRef) in a small core module; navigation by file then mirrors the routes.

findings.issue: The routeLoader$ + status(404) + NotFound + head/resolveValue boilerplate is repeated nearly identically in four route files.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable in Qwik City (it's the idiomatic pattern), but a tiny shared helper for the head title resolution and 404 wrapper would trim each route to its unique markup.

findings.issue: team.ts mixes pure normalization (parseTeam/normalizeTeam), coverage math, and browser document.cookie manipulation in one module imported by both server and client code.
findings.suggestion: Keep the shared pure module and move saveTeamCookie into a small client-only module (e.g. lib/team-cookie.ts); the existing comment shows the author was aware of the trade-off.

findings.issue: spriteUrl hardcodes the media path pattern, so while the API base is centralized in api.ts, knowledge of the sprite URL scheme is split across api.ts (base) and data.ts (path shape).
findings.suggestion: Fine as is; if media rules ever change, consider moving sprite/artwork URL construction into api.ts next to apiBase so all URL knowledge lives together.

findings.issue: Shared UI components import their prop types from ~/lib/data, a server-only data module, coupling the component layer's type surface to the server layer.
findings.suggestion: Hoist shared display types (Card, TypeRef, EvolutionNode) into a types-only module (e.g. lib/types.ts) that both data.ts and components import from.

summary: This is a well-layered, idiomatic Qwik City 1.20 codebase: transport/caching in api.ts, per-page server builders in data.ts, thin routes over reusable components, and an explicit cookie-based client/server seam for team state. Editability is good — features map to one route file plus one data function, and the API base URL is a single function — but the shared Pokémon Card shape is constructed in three separate places, so card-level changes (sprites, sorting) ripple. The only structural drag is data.ts being a 449-line god module that could be split per domain.
